title: 2025-604 primary-source mechanisms and strategic context
body:
# 2025-604 — Quixilver: The Flush; separate offseason Quixshot

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-cad-code-release-for-our-2025-robot-the-flush/502824

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## The Flush in-season release · drivetrain

### Published construction or code

29-inch square chassis with WCP X2i modules and a 5.9:1 drive ratio; the team optimized for roughly 18-foot average sprint distance. Protective panels isolate electronics from falling coral.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Stability at high reach and the expected travel distance drive the stated choices.

### Engineering interpretation

Optimize acceleration and usable travel under the expected route distribution, rather than unloaded top speed alone. A larger support polygon can help a reaching superstructure while increasing congestion exposure. The published dimensions and ratio are a configuration snapshot; they do not prove the same ratio is best for 1833 or a different game.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## The Flush elevator and arm · scoring

### Published construction or code

Single-stage elevator uses 2x2 uprights, cross bracing and chain drive on both sides. The release gives two Kraken X60s, 3:1 and 28 inches of motion; stator limits increased from 40A to 80A. The arm is rigidly tied side-to-side and its gearbox shimmed; the team describes detuning and reducing the drive to one motor at 100A to avoid tipping.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Rigidity, low backlash and precise automated control are explicit priorities.

### Engineering interpretation

Motor count and theoretical joint acceleration cannot be separated from robot stability. Dual-sided chain drive addresses carriage twist, while a rigid camera mount helps relate vision measurements to mechanism geometry. Preserve the stated revisions and the release’s mixed original/final motor annotations; do not silently combine every number into one certified event configuration.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## The Flush station funnel and gripper · intake

### Published construction or code

A full-width 4mm corrugated-plastic funnel loads from three sides through separately powered rollers. The gripper has independently powered left/right rollers, four coral rollers and two algae rollers, plus an open top.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team wanted tolerant loading, horizontal L1 packing and precise placement. The open top avoids reef entanglement and permits a shallower coral release angle.

### Engineering interpretation

A funnel can absorb human-player variability while the gripper controls the final release. Independent sides support a different L1 placement policy rather than merely increasing raw roller power. This is an architectural option for a station-fed role, not evidence that floor coral pickup was unnecessary for every alliance. Corrugated plastic stiffness, folding and clearances must be evaluated in the installed package.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## The Flush climb/funnel interface · endgame

### Published construction or code

The release describes a roughly 3.5-pound climber including motor and gearbox, stowed below the funnel, surgical-tubing extension and a 15:1 winch with a 2:1 pulley. A rear funnel ramp unfolds to clear the cage and climb.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Compact packaging preserves the loading system while providing cage engagement tolerance.

### Engineering interpretation

The climb is coupled to the funnel’s motion and the loaded robot CG. A compact mechanism is not necessarily easy to approach under traffic; validate capture, retraction and failures with the actual funnel and piece state. These are team-reported design quantities, not measured masses or an exhaustive installed-version history.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## The Flush and separate Quixshot offseason machine · controls

### Published construction or code

The Flush uses predictive target selection, smooth handover from driver motion, reef-clearance sequencing and separate local/global localization. The team reports 547/549 L2-L4 coral placements over its last two events. Quixshot is a distinct offseason coral launcher with manually tuned launch velocity differentials and a one-time intake deploy latch.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team reports that packaging a ground pickup with the in-season climber became difficult, so the compatible pickup was instead installed on the offseason launcher.

### Engineering interpretation

Do not attach Quixshot’s launcher to the in-season elevator robot. The 99.6% is a bounded team-reported placement statistic, not full-match reliability or 99.6% for every task. The published offseason answer says it did not deep-climb or handle algae at that point. The strongest transferable lesson is a deliberate interface and packaging trade, not the assertion that launching always beats placing.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Distinct offseason machine

Quixshot is a separate robot. The team’s July reply explains that a ground intake intended for the in-season machine conflicted with climber packaging and was installed on the launcher instead. Launch velocity differentials were manually tuned. The first offseason answer explicitly says no algae or deep climb at that point. Do not combine the two robots into one imaginary in-season architecture. Source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2025-offseason-robot-quixshot/504607/55

## Evidence limits

- Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.
- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.

# 2026-604 — Quixilver: Toploader

Primary source: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-604-quixilver-2026-robot-cad-and-code-release/524289

Reviewed 2026-10-26. This is a source-bounded technical study. Construction, stated intent, interpretation and unresolved evidence are separate.

## Toploader DPC serializer · transfer

### Published construction or code

A rotating capture mechanism scoops fuel from a circular plywood bucket. Rotation and up-feed have separate motors; side rollers use omni wheels. Successive fuel pushes through a corrugated-plastic tube shaped by printed ends. The bucket separates into two sections for service.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team identified serialization as the limiting process and designed the robot around it. Independent drives allow software adjustment of rotation versus up-feed.

### Engineering interpretation

The capture point moves to available fuel rather than relying solely on gravity bringing fuel to a stationary throat. Independent feed authority can help tune pile interaction and column delivery separately, but the release does not establish a universal motor-ratio setting. Bucket geometry, turret support and electronics access are part of the same flow system. Prototype rates of about 15 BPS single-stream and 23 BPS full-width are comparison claims, not sustained match scoring rates.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader chassis · drivetrain

### Published construction or code

A 27-inch square frame preserves circular bucket area without custom swerves or chamfered corners. Internal bars protect battery and module compartments; rear bumper mounts integrate armor for serializer protection.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Maximize the serializer’s available area with manufacturable hardware and protect internal mechanisms.

### Engineering interpretation

This is an explicit packaging choice. It sacrifices some geometric freedom to keep the central circular feed volume useful with standard drive components. Frame perimeter, usable interior area and turret swept volume must be compared together. The team separately describes bump-only autonomous constraints; no unreviewed trench state or chassis specification should be inferred.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader inset turret · scoring

### Published construction or code

The turret is supported from above and packaged to reduce swept volume. Its sliding bearing stacks polycarbonate and aluminum plates; printed PETG spacers set clearance empirically and grease reduces friction.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Moving scoring and feeding were judged worth a lower single-stream ceiling; small swept volume preserves hopper capacity and flow.

### Engineering interpretation

A turret changes more than aiming. Its supports and swept envelope can obstruct fuel entering the serializer, so a nominal capacity comparison that ignores the moving assembly is incomplete. This release supports a manufacturable impact-tolerant bearing concept, not exact dimensions, a universal bearing preload or independently verified shot accuracy. The team’s rate trade is tied to its intended moving role.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader independently deployed arms · intake

### Published construction or code

Each intake arm uses an X44 deploy motor. Protected motors belt-drive compliant dead-axle polycarbonate rollers with silicone tubing and TPU pulley plugs. TPU belt supports retain the belts during deflection. A one-time kicker deploy uses surgical tubing and flexible plugs/string.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The team explicitly connects independent deployment to eliminating the mechanically linked 2024 chain failure. Polycarbonate was preferred over SRPP to avoid permanent deformation changing belt centers.

### Engineering interpretation

Compliance must preserve transmission function, not just prevent fracture. A flexible arm changes belt geometry under load; supporting the belt during that motion is an integral part of the architecture. The team reports that TPU replaced brittle PETG roller plugs, with 100% infill and four-wall printing, and that wear still requires replacement every one or two events. Repairable consumables are not maintenance-free hardware.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader linked sliding hopper · intake

### Published construction or code

Intake deployment extends a sliding hopper; surgical tubing retracts it. Two laminated layers of corrugated plastic provide stiffness. Slots are reinforced with 0.090-inch polycarbonate sandwiched between sheets; panels use tape and adhesive for replacement.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

The publication emphasizes low mass, robust sliding and easy manufacture/repair with limited router access.

### Engineering interpretation

This is a specific example of an intake–storage interface, useful to 1833’s morph chart. Linking deployment reduces independent actuation but also links faults and operating states. Slot reinforcement addresses local bearing and deformation loads that a generic corrugated-plastic wall description misses. Capacity, deflection and passage access should be measured in each loaded state; no unverified hopper capacity is assigned here.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader readiness and localization · controls

### Published construction or code

Scoring requires launch velocity, launch angle and turret yaw within tolerance plus a recent image with at least two tags. The serializer pauses when readiness fails. PhotonVision MultiTag selects camera poses using hub/total tag visibility and rejects old or ambiguous poses.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

Single-driver operation reduces communication overhead; automated gating is intended to release fuel only from useful launch states.

### Engineering interpretation

Feed interruption is an intentional interface between aiming and serialization, not automatically a jam. A high mechanical BPS ceiling is useful only while readiness remains true. Logging the reason for each gating interruption would distinguish vision starvation, aim error and actual feed trouble. The release does not demonstrate those duty fractions or an electrical diagnosis of every stop.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Toploader partner-aware bump autonomous · controls

### Published construction or code

The team describes timestamping partner paths, targeting leftover fuel after the trench race, using reusable path partials and adjustable pauses without redeployment. A Pac-Man routine is identified at NorCal DCMP playoff match 1.

### Stated rationale and boundaries

A bump-only robot was expected to reach midfield later; route selection was built around shorter partners rather than competing for the same initial race.

### Engineering interpretation

Architectural limitations can become planning inputs instead of being hidden by an ideal autonomous animation. Preserve the team’s distinction between pre-Champs crossing rules and later rules, and between experiments and actually used routines. A clever path is not proof every prototype routine competed. The release does not establish a tower mechanism; absence from the selected technical sections remains unknown, not certified absence.

### Validation still required

Verify the installed configuration and interfaces against the original publication/CAD; prototype full acquisition-to-output cycles, recovery and service access under the intended loaded and defended conditions. These tests are proposed, not performed.

## Evidence limits

- Selected primary publications/code reviewed; exact per-event installation and exhaustive intermediate revisions remain unresolved.
- Four previously blocked source originals (2023 robot photo; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper CAD views) were recovered through normal browser downloads on 2026-10-26 and inspected. Whole-robot source views are not exhaustive mechanism or event-version certification.


## Recovered original source images · 2026-10-26

The earlier direct-download failures are resolved. These are unchanged originals from the team release; the labels below are editorial retrieval aids. Inspect the full view before borrowing packaging ideas. Exact dimensions, hidden construction and match performance require independent source evidence.

title: 1833 supplied task and subsystem research workflow
body:
# 1833’s supplied 2026 design workflow

The original workbook and PDF are preserved under team1833/. Their statements are historical team planning, not validated game rules or independent mechanism measurements. Cell-level and PDF-page text exports permit exact retrieval. No source workbook or PDF was edited.

The workbook contains parallel group task lists, numeric priority/difficulty judgments, formulas multiplying those ordinal values, and a cleaned must/might/won’t list. Some sheets have inconsistent priority scales. The cleaned list’s repeated “No” final-decision cells must not be interpreted as rejecting every must-do task. Group 4 even distinguishes autonomous climb priority in qualifications versus eliminations. Keep group opinions and later decisions separate instead of silently averaging them into a consensus.

The PDF maps requirements into intake, storage, shooter, climb, electrical and chassis concepts. It records historical mechanism references, pros/cons and open prototype questions about compression and roller materials. It explicitly asks for service access, wire protection and mechanical/electrical compatibility. The shooter page contains proposed distances, angles and velocities; these are unverified calculations, with launch-height, drag and other assumptions needing reconstruction before reuse. References such as 2020 spindexer slot capacity must not become universal capacity limits for 2026 bulk serializers.

For the agent: reproduce the task-to-requirement-to-concept chain, preserve alternatives and open tests, and distinguish kickoff judgments from later evidence. The early climb priorities are historical inputs; the user’s later correction and tower-only data establish a fuel-first default for the studied 2026 competitive context. Do not overwrite the original documents to make hindsight look like the initial decision. A future task sheet should carry rule revision, phase, partner assumptions, expected contribution, ordinal priority meaning, development cost, evidence and decision rationale. A mechanism comparison should identify which requirement it serves and what observation would change the choice.


## Required 1833 task sheet

For each new game/manual analysis, material rules revision or new/revised robot design brief, fill a fresh copy of [the one-sheet template](../../team1833/1833_Task_List_Template.xlsx). Follow `docs/TASK_LIST_PROTOCOL.md` and `team1833/task_template_schema.json`, with all paths resolved from the corpus root. The template includes task outcome, phase, points/enabling value, priority, difficulty, recommendation, rationale, alliance dependencies, acceptance target, exact rule/source, uncertainty/test and separate human decision. No group tabs; no inherited season-specific decisions. Four previously blocked 604 image originals are now recovered and embedded (2023 robot; 2026 serializer, intake and hopper).


## 1833 elite architecture and decision-quality edition

The owner requires an Einstein-level primary contributor, never a support-only design, and no turret. Relatively simple mechanisms should be optimized for elite output. Historical research remains available, including turret robots and complementary match assignments; those are not permission to violate this design brief. Read `docs/1833_DESIGN_DOCTRINE.md`, `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, `docs/1833_OPTIMIZATION_REFERENCES.md` and `docs/evaluations/DUNKTANK_REVIEW_2026-10-26.md`. ## PDF page 3

 
Requirements (Which of the Goals does this Complete?):  
●​ Ferrying from neutral zone 
●​ Scoring into hub 
●​ Holding pieces  
●​ Scoring as much fuel as possible as quick as possible (shorten cycle times) 
 
 
Concepts:  
●​ Fuel hopper; Similar to 1678 and 254 2017, open top that can also take from rollers on 
the base 
○​ Pros: 
■​ Lots of storage, could store a good bit of fuel, (Likely upwards of 40-50 
fuel, (thanks Adi RI3D concept holding around 50 fuel ))  
■​ Decently simple, like would rank this at a middle/medium difficulty 
■​ Works really well with outpost/human player station intaking due to open 
top, just pour as many as possible in and start shooting when at hub (and 
its active) 
■​ Fastest net cycle time (longer to fill, more to score) 
○​ Cons:  
■​ Takes up a lot of room on robot 
■​ Possible jams (more likely than other options) 
■​ A lot of belts/rollers to function 
■​ If it expands past the frame perimeter its going to get hit 
■​ Could cause issues going under trenches, have to keep it shorter or find a 
way to fold 
●​ Spindexer; 1690 2020 
○​ Pros: 
■​ Less chance of jams (slots for fuel) 
■​ Efficient 
○​ Cons: 
■​ Limited fuel storage max 5 fuel 
■​ Takes up decent bit of space  
■​ Complex 
■​ Requires additional pathing/almost a second mini indexer to get to 
shooter (tower) 
●​ “S- curve” Indexer; 2910 2021 
○​ Pros: 
■​ Takes up smaller space  
■​ Unlikely to jam, fuel follows a rigid path 
■​ Pretty simple 
○​ Cons: 
■​ Less fuel storage, 3 fuel max (maybe 4 but it would be difficult and the 
curve would be have to be pretty harsh (and tall)) 
●​ Multi roller indexer (Vertical and horizontal); 4414 2021 


## PDF page 4

 
○​ Pros:  
■​ Significantly less space taken up on robot 
■​ Really simple 
○​ Cons: 
■​ Little to no storage for fuel, max 1-2 fuel (likely 1) 
■​ Medium jam possibility (2nd most likely to jam) 
■​ Slow cycle times (due to limited fuel) 
 
●​ Combo spindexer and hopper; 1986 2017 
 
1986 Team Titanium 2017 Robot Reveal
○​ Pros: 
■​ Lots of storage space (roughly equal to just the spindexer idea, maybe -1 
or 2 fuel) 
■​ Not more complicated than the ideas individually, just basically a 
spindexer with hopper walls 
■​ Works with both ground intake and outpost intake from top 
■​ Cuts the amount of rollers/belts needed for just the hopper (replaces that 
with the spindexer portion) 
■​ Fast net cycle time (long reload but more ammo) 
■​ (seems) very efficient  
○​ Cons: 
■​ Still takes up a lot of room on robot 
■​ Still needs booster/ mini indexer to go to the shooter 
■​ Jams would be questionable???? (Taking most likely to jam and least 
likely to jam and putting them together so im unsure) 
■​ Expansion would still be a concern

title: 1833 mandatory single-sheet task-list completion protocol
body:
> Owner constraints: no pneumatics; no turrets; no support-only architecture. Historical scope and future 2018/2019 roadmap: `docs/1833_ACTUATION_AND_HISTORY_SCOPE.md` from corpus root.

> Owner correction: prioritize independently achievable RP and essential scoring independence. Physical iteration is extremely expensive; use proportionate analytical checks and targeted tests. Read `docs/1833_SOLO_RP_AND_DECISION_ECONOMICS.md` from corpus root.

> 1833 override: elite primary-contributor architecture; no support-only robot; no turret. Apply `docs/1833_DESIGN_DOCTRINE.md` and `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` from corpus root.

# 1833 required task-list protocol

## Required deliverable and trigger

For every new-season manual analysis, material rules revision, or new/revised robot design brief, fill a fresh copy of `team1833/1833_Task_List_Template.xlsx` before presenting the final architecture recommendation. The required output is a populated workbook with exactly one worksheet, `Task List`. Do not create group tabs. The blank canonical template must remain blank. Save the populated copy under a dated season-and-brief filename; preserve previous analyses so changed priorities can be explained. For a small revision, revise a copy of the previous sheet and identify the changed assumption or rule and its consequences in the rationale. The template is a work product requirement, not a guarantee that a model will obey without being given this protocol.

## Establish the decision context

Fill the six metadata inputs C2:H7: season/game; exact manual revision and governing source URL; target event, week and competition stage; expected alliance roles and opponent assumptions; 1833's time, people, fabrication, budget, robot packaging, practice and maintenance constraints; and agent/date/human review status. Unknown inputs must be explicitly marked unknown with the assumption used provisionally. Historical EPA, alliance scores and Worlds examples do not substitute for the current manual or team constraints. If these are not available, produce a provisional sheet and identify the missing inputs rather than inventing them.

## Enumerate the work before choosing mechanisms

Use one actionable task or required outcome per row, beginning at row 13. Cover every legal task and enabling capability that could matter: mobility and traversal, acquisition, storage and transfer, resource control, scoring, autonomous, endgame, alignment/sensing, defense/support, and other legal actions. These are starter categories, not mandatory robot subsystems. Add or rename categories when the game requires it. Record an excluded or inapplicable task with the reason instead of silently omitting it. Split the same task into separate rows when autonomous/teleop, event stage, alliance role, field location or game state changes its value materially. Keep a functional task such as collecting floor pieces separate from an architecture proposal such as a slapdown intake; mechanisms are evaluated after the functional priorities are stated.

Columns A–N are defined in `team1833/task_template_schema.json` and in the worksheet header. For each occupied task row, complete A–F and H–M; G is calculated. Use N/A plus a reason where a field truly does not apply, and unknown plus a smallest decision-changing test where evidence is missing. Column N is reserved for an actual human decision/rationale: leave blank or label pending human review until 1833 supplies a decision. Never fabricate human approval. Preserve the user's explicit corrections as attributed context alongside their date and scope.

## Give priorities a defensible meaning

Priority 1 means essential to the rule-derived elite primary-contributor objective, before architecture selection; 2 means valuable; 3 means optional. Difficulty uses the team's relative Fibonacci scale: 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21. Explain the basis of both judgments in Why / tradeoff. Do not treat the product P×D as an objective ranking, a points-per-effort model or a decision rule. The supplied original workbook used priority times difficulty; this template retains that discussion aid without claiming it captures strategic value. A difficult must-do can remain a must-do. A high-point action can be unnecessary for this robot when an alliance partner covers it. Enabling tasks and denial can be valuable without directly scoring points.

Use the Agent recommendation dropdown: Must do, Might do, Won’t do, or Needs discussion. State the opportunity cost, partner dependency, game-state conditions and reliability assumptions that could change it. Column D should distinguish rule points from inferred enabling value; include timing, capacity, accuracy or probability conditions when quantified. Do not invent numeric precision when the data supports only a qualitative judgment.

## Make each recommendation testable and traceable

Acceptance target / units must describe a measurable functional outcome under specified conditions, or explicitly say the target is not yet established. Examples include loaded collection success, release accuracy at a stated location, usable capacity with the mechanism swept envelope, sustained throughput including acquisition and readiness interruptions, or recovery time after a jam. These examples are not requirements or performed tests. Record the rule number/section/page and revision, and the exact source or corpus locator behind each factual claim. Clearly distinguish official rules, team-reported performance, attributed commentary, 1833's judgment and agent inference. Unknowns / smallest test should identify what observation or prototype result could change the priority or architecture.

After filling the sheet, compare at least two coherent architectures against the same prioritized tasks and constraints. Cite historical inspiration by year/team/version and inspect the whole acquisition-to-output interface. Feed architecture findings back into the sheet when they change difficulty, dependencies or acceptance criteria. Preserve both the initial reason and the reason for the revision. Do not jump from famous team names to compatibility claims.

## Workbook handling and completion gate

The starter table `RobotTasks` occupies A12:N92, providing 80 task rows. It is a starting capacity, not a task limit. If more rows are needed, insert rows within/at the end of the table and extend the table, G formulas, E/F/H validations and summary ranges in B10/E10/H10/K10 to include every occupied row; move the provenance footer below the table. Do not add another worksheet. Keep frozen headings and task columns. G must remain blank until task, priority and difficulty are supplied. Summary counts count only the named statuses; verify no recommendation is left on an unused row and no placeholder category row is counted as a task.

Before delivering, check exactly one sheet, correct manual revision, all task categories considered, all occupied rows documented, no invented decisions, formulas recalculated, no spreadsheet errors, and source locators preserved. Unresolved items may remain explicitly unresolved; their existence must be reflected in the confidence and proposed tests. Deliver the filled workbook with the design analysis. A prose task list alone does not satisfy the user's requested workflow.

## Provenance

This template adapts the user's supplied `team1833/task_list_2026.xlsx`, particularly its cleaned task list and the group sheets' priority/difficulty fields, without reproducing the group tabs or inheriting the original season's priorities. `team1833/mechanical_research_2026.pdf` remains a separate input to mechanism brainstorming. Historical kickoff choices and later strategic corrections retain their original context; the template does not rewrite them as current universal priorities.


## Substantive completion gate added after the DunkTank review

Task-specific dependencies, justified difficulty, distinct unknown/test/decision consequences, and consistent screening versus release requirements are mandatory. Repeated generic filler does not satisfy a field. A field threshold is not an onboard capacity mandate. Compare capacities and fixed/expanding storage, perform common-assumption match modeling, and apply the owner constraints before final recommendation. Run `scripts/audit_task_workbook.py` and the design-review validator; human review remains necessary. Follow `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md` for detailed requirements.

title: 1833 owner mandate: elite primary contributor, no support architecture, no turret
body:
> Owner constraints: no pneumatics; no turrets; no support-only architecture. Historical scope and future 2018/2019 roadmap: `docs/1833_ACTUATION_AND_HISTORY_SCOPE.md` from corpus root.

> Owner correction: prioritize independently achievable RP and essential scoring independence. Physical iteration is extremely expensive; use proportionate analytical checks and targeted tests. Read `docs/1833_SOLO_RP_AND_DECISION_ECONOMICS.md` from corpus root.

# 1833 design mandate — owner instruction, 2026-10-26

## Binding design brief

Design to be the best robot on the field: an Einstein-level primary contributor, alliance-captain or elite first-round caliber. Never propose a support-role robot as 1833's architecture. Never propose a turret. Favor relatively simple mechanisms that achieve elite effectiveness through execution, acquisition, sustained throughput, autonomous, driving, controls, reliability, serviceability and extensive optimization. These are explicit user constraints, not conclusions inferred from EPA or a generic small-team stereotype. Only a later explicit user instruction can change them. Do not repeatedly ask to relax them.

Primary contribution is an objective to substantiate, not a guarantee of a future result or an instruction to do every available task. Rank functions by contribution to winning and eliminate low-value complexity. A dominant scorer can play defense or a complementary assignment in a particular match; that does not turn its architecture into a deliberately limited third robot. Preserve historical specialist examples, including 2025 parallel L1/algae assignments, as knowledge about alliance optimization. They are not authorization to cap 1833's own architecture at a support role.

For this profile, turret means a dedicated azimuth/yaw aiming assembly for the scoring mechanism. A chassis-aimed launcher can still have an adjustable hood, elevation pivot or other game-required motion if justified. Explain the cost of chassis aiming, angular acceleration, shot readiness, defender interaction and positioning. Do not disguise a turret under a different name, or delete useful historical turret research: its intake, feed, sensors and failure histories may still be transferable.

The 2027 game is unknown in this analysis. Do not prescribe a 2026 drum, a 2024 low chassis or any historical geometry before reading its rules and strategic constraints. Transfer the optimization approach, not an unexamined shape. A game requiring vertical reach may justify an elevator even though a short chassis worked in another game.

## Ambition grounded in the team's stated history

The owner reports that 1833 peaked at eighth worldwide EPA in 2026, was around 35th at this instruction, and was top 75 worldwide during 2025. Treat these as owner-reported dated context; peak date, ranking cohort and model version were not supplied. The included older mirror snapshot instead contains 2026 rank 36 / EPA 233.53 and 2025 rank 130 / EPA 73.05. Do not silently overwrite either record, mistake an end/snapshot rank for a historical peak, or infer a permanent capability limit from a different snapshot. Live ranking pages/API were not successfully available in this research pass. Official 2026 records confirm Newton Division Finalist; the alliance record identifies 1833 as captain of alliance 5 with 930, 180 and 3966. This supports treating 1833 as an established high-performing team, while actual current shop/time constraints remain inputs to obtain.

## Alliance selection and design ceiling

The owner's warning is that an excellent narrow specialist may survive the first selection round and become the first available second-round pick of alliance 8, instead of joining a leading alliance. The 2026 official manual section 10.6.1 confirms first-round order 1→8 and second-round order 8→1; section 13.2 adds Worlds' third round 1→8 and four-team rosters with three starters. This is an incentive to build an independently valuable leading robot, not a deterministic theorem about draft outcomes. Captains, first picks, scouting judgments, availability, declines, autonomous compatibility and game-specific marginal value affect actual choices; a first-round pick list is not necessarily EPA order. Check the next season's rules rather than assuming the format persists.

Do not optimize 1833 merely to be the best remaining specialist. Analyze qualification ranking power, individual offensive production, autonomous ownership of contested resources, contribution with ordinary partners, and ceiling alongside elite partners. Report why the design would plausibly be attractive as a captain or first-round partner. Do not invent a numerical probability of an Einstein appearance or draft position.

## Simplicity means removing costs while retaining output

Compare mechanisms by actuators, coupled states, interfaces, tolerance sensitivity, manufacturing burden, software commissioning, driver demands, service operations and development time—not silhouette or motor count alone. A simple-looking elevator can hide elaborate alignment, handoff, vacuum or trajectory control. Reduced moving inertia, reliable acquisition and short dead time can produce elite output without decorative complexity. Conversely, a necessary capability must not be omitted merely to make the robot look simple.

The specific exemplars and their limits are researched in `docs/1833_OPTIMIZATION_REFERENCES.md`. 7769's jam remedy is evidence that stronger feed is not automatically better; its rack failures prohibit treating its entire mechanism as perfected. Orbit's compact 2024 robot combined low packaging with substantial controls and refinement. OP 2025 used familiar high-level functions but considerable integration. Orbit 2025 used a differential transmission and vacuum system with real maintenance and control costs. The owner's comparison of 1261 with Orbit is an attributed diagnostic lead, not a verified causal account of another team's failures.

## Required decision outputs

Read `docs/DESIGN_REVIEW_PROTOCOL.md`, complete the one-sheet task workbook, and supply the evidence package specified by `team1833/design_review_schema.json`. Compare credible non-turret primary-contributor architectures with common assumptions before recommending one. If decisive information is missing, recommend a provisional candidate and the next test, rather than declaring superiority without analysis. Run the structural checks, apply the 100-point rubric, and disclose unperformed experiments and unverified claims. Passing a file validator does not establish robot quality or model intelligence.

## Sources

- Owner instruction in this conversation, 2026-10-26: authoritative for preferences and ambition; reported performance claims retain attribution.
- https://firstfrc.blob.core.windows.net/frc2026/Manual/HTML/2026GameManual.htm — sections 10.6.1 and 13.2.
- https://frc-events.firstinspires.org/2026/team/1833 — division finalist record.
- https://www.thebluealliance.com/event/2026new — alliance membership.
- `tables/season_epa.jsonl` — retained historical mirror snapshot; not a newly verified live rank.

title: 1833 architecture decision protocol: models, capacity, dependencies and acceptance
body:
> Owner constraints: no pneumatics; no turrets; no support-only architecture. Historical scope and future 2018/2019 roadmap: `docs/1833_ACTUATION_AND_HISTORY_SCOPE.md` from corpus root.

> Owner correction: prioritize independently achievable RP and essential scoring independence. Physical iteration is extremely expensive; use proportionate analytical checks and targeted tests. Read `docs/1833_SOLO_RP_AND_DECISION_ECONOMICS.md` from corpus root.

# Architecture decision review and task quality protocol

This protocol addresses the DunkTank output reviewed on 2026-10-26. The historical artifact earned 68/100 under the recorded rubric; that is a reviewer assessment, not a model benchmark. The new 1833 constraints also make its support-only baseline unacceptable as a current recommendation. Do not change its original score retroactively or present an untested replacement design as a demonstrated improvement.

## 1. Establish functional priorities before choosing a role or mechanism

Start with rule-derived actions and constraints, including autonomous, primary scoring, enabling resource flow, endgame and denial. Record phase and game-state effects before specializing an architecture. Identify what would make 1833 the strongest primary contributor. Map the objective into measurable useful outcomes; do not fill the task sheet with priorities that merely restate a preselected specialist role. Keep outcome tasks, implementation concepts, compliance constraints and alliance-wide results distinct. Extra rows are not evidence of comprehensive understanding. Retain one sheet; use labeled rows or a hierarchy inside that sheet rather than group tabs.

Record initial neutral functional priorities and the reasons for any changes after architecture comparison. A team's assignment alongside exceptional partners is a scenario, not proof that the robot should depend on those partners for fundamental scoring. Follow the binding no-support and no-turret constraints in `docs/1833_DESIGN_DOCTRINE.md`.

## 2. Model the game as state and flow

Identify inventories, locations, capacity/weight thresholds, scoring eligibility, occupied goals, possession, reload/discharge behavior, deadlines and final evaluation conditions. Model autonomous, transition and endgame separately where the rules differ. Opening a return chute can change feasible sustained flow, but does not establish that returned pieces are accessible or instantly reusable. Include return delay, collection success, route interference and control latency. Check rule-specific settling/scoring cutoffs rather than applying an invented universal end timestamp.

For each candidate, construct a timed match/resource model under at least three named scenarios: ordinary or weak partners; strong partners; and elite defended play. The same partner capabilities, field rules, opponent assumptions and external supply must apply to every candidate within a scenario. Show acquisition, travel, alignment, release, recovery and waiting separately, and document which operations overlap. Use measured or sourced values when available; otherwise use explicitly labeled plausible ranges and sensitivity analysis. Unknown inputs cannot silently become optimistic constants. Do not add overlapping time costs twice or count the same enabled alliance points as multiple robots' individual output.

Calculate whole-alliance output and compare the counterfactual replacement: same partners, different 1833 architecture. Report direct contribution, enabled contribution, denied contribution and opportunity cost separately, with interactions explained. A shared multiplier can help the opponent. A hostile reset may enable them to score again. Evaluate per-goal final-state recovery instead of a binary full-refill test. A maximum possible score or denial is not an expected match result.

## 3. Compare capacity and deployment choices explicitly

A field threshold is not automatically an onboard capacity requirement. Compare at least three plausible capacities or storage arrangements spanning the proposed choice. For a 100-piece cumulative threshold, 50/75/100/150 are illustrative candidates, not prescribed targets. Consider existing target inventory, multiple deliveries, collection delay, cross-field distance, throughput, spill, usable packing and loaded maneuverability. Compare fixed versus expanding storage before adding expansion. Record what packing fraction means and reserve volume for conveyors, structure, supports, electronics, moving swept volume and trapped pieces.

Use deliverable capacity under stated motion and wear conditions. If delivery efficiency is eta, capacity C and residual r, account for losses without double-counting them; a simplified effective delivery estimate C*eta-r must state its assumptions. A 100-count load with 98% retention cannot guarantee 100 delivered. If the field threshold is measured by weight, piece counts are a proxy requiring tolerance and calibration rather than a certified exact trigger. Inventory sensing and target-state sensing are distinct problems.

## 4. Select between credible complete candidates

Compare at least two viable non-turret primary-contributor architectures. Do not use an intentionally weak alternative to justify a preferred concept. Compare mission output, controllability, defended performance, autonomous, loaded dynamics, resources, complexity and development time using common assumptions. A high-level sketch or bounded layout is sufficient at this stage; exact fabrication drawings and invented motor ratios are not required.

Establish the physical envelope: legal start/deployed dimensions, ground transition, storage volume, lift to outlet, entry aperture, collision/swept volumes, electrical access and loaded CG. Label dimensions measured from governing CAD separately from provisional allocations. Resolve cheap geometry questions before a large prototype. Identify which values could reverse the choice, show those sensitivities, and define fallback milestones.

An original mechanism is allowed without a famous reference. Its essential interfaces still need a causal explanation and a test. For borrowed mechanisms verify year/team/version, game-piece diameter/material/deformability and competition hardware legality. The 2022 Rapid React cargo diameter is 9.5 inches, not 7 inches. Never transfer compression, traction or roller speed merely because both objects are called balls. Keep representative source images and locators available to the next reviewer; claim visual review only when actually performed.

## 5. Make the task workbook substantive

Every occupied row must carry a task-specific dependency and rationale. Identify actual predecessor tasks or external conditions, relevant mechanism interfaces, and effects of failure. Repeated generic statements about coordination or unverified CAD do not satisfy this requirement. Explain difficulty using a consistent basis such as interfaces, maturity, tolerance, manufacturing and commissioning. Do not pretend the Fibonacci scale is a calibrated numeric effort estimate. Distinguish no relevant task (N/A) from a real task excluded from the robot.

Column K contains an authoritative acceptance requirement or a clearly unresolved target. Column M identifies the unknown, the test that resolves it, and the decision it changes; merely copying K after an introductory sentence is insufficient. Distinguish screening targets from release criteria explicitly. Preserve row/requirement IDs in the design record so cross-row conflicts can be reconciled. If one row allows two residual balls and another requires a guaranteed 100-ball delivery from a 100-ball load, label the former as intermediate screening and prevent release until the system target is met.

Keep agent recommendations and human decisions separate. Check summary formulas, caches, validations and occupied-row coverage. Run `python scripts/audit_task_workbook.py PATH.xlsx`; its duplicate-field warnings require human review, not automatic deletion of legitimately shared dependencies. It cannot validate physics or infer the semantic consistency of every target.

## 6. Test only where the value justifies the iteration cost

First verify rules and field apertures, then use inexpensive envelope and analytical checks. Only where consequential uncertainty remains, test the cheapest capacity/transition or one-lane geometry that can change the choice. Then prototype representative loaded flow, sensing and reversal; integrate at full capacity when the smaller tests support it. Complete defended/dynamic trials and practice validation before calling the system competition-ready. State hypothesis, conditions, sample size, measured quantities, screening/release target, and decision consequence for each test. A proposed 20/20 result is an acceptance target, not measured evidence or a statistical reliability guarantee.

## 7. Deliver and preserve the decision

Deliver the populated single-sheet workbook; one selected architecture and the complete alternatives comparison; quantitative scenario/capacity results with input provenance; physical envelope; exact reference locators/images; and prioritized open tests. Maintain assumptions, decisions, rejected alternatives, user corrections and test results in a dated design record. Fill `examples/design_review_skeleton.json` as a machine-readable summary and run `python scripts/validate_design_review.py FILE.json`. Apply `agent/design_rubric.json` with evidence for each score. The no-support and no-turret gates take precedence over a high numeric score. Validation is structural; a human must judge whether inputs and conclusions are credible.


## Solo ranking capability and proportional evidence

For a new architecture, explicitly map each ranking objective to independent capability or external prerequisites and quantify the individually achievable route with margin. Include a passive-partner stress case in addition to ordinary/elite alliance comparisons. Complete the solo RP record and validation economics; the latter must identify decision consequences, expected costs, cheapest evidence and stopping rules. A bounded improvement can use a short comparison and update only affected task rows, rather than repeating full CAD or model development. See `docs/1833_SOLO_RP_AND_DECISION_ECONOMICS.md` for the owner's actual four-lane decision and the proportionate process.

title: 1833 optimization exemplars: 7769, Orbit, OP and Robo Lions
body:
# Elite output from relatively simple concepts — research synthesis

Research date: 2026-10-26 America/New_York. This synthesis combines newly checked primary posts, the existing source-bounded corpus studies, the OP binder text, official event/rule records and explicitly attributed owner observations. Primary-source facts and our transfer analysis remain separate. No new full visual interview watch or exhaustive CAD audit is claimed. Read the complete historical robot packets before importing mechanism dimensions.

## 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history

Primary facts: the release describes a two-chamber shooter revised to a 2.75-width configuration, almost 70 nominal capacity and typically 50–60 in play. Team replies describe a static hood avoiding an exposed hood belt, and a feed jam corrected by stopping the lower indexing rollers. They also report rack-tooth breakage that persisted despite current-limit mitigation, with spares and repairs needed. Their linked technical slides currently display that the file was deleted. Those slides were not read. The retained mirror snapshot ranks 7769 fourth worldwide at EPA 309.29; it is a dated snapshot, not live verification. Official event results support an elite competitive season.

1833 transfer analysis: the useful principle is that usable match throughput is a system property. More capacity can add loaded inertia, acquisition dwell and feed pressure. More powered contact can make a congested path worse. Begin with a clear hypothesis about the limiting stage, instrument occupancy and delay at each transition, and change one stage before attributing a scoring gain. Test the near-empty, partly full and fully packed states separately. Under a defended shot, distinguish lost aim time, inaccessible geometry, supply starvation and a genuine mechanical jam. A simple hood can reduce interfaces and service work, but its advantages depend on the scoring aperture and collision environment of the new game.

The rack failure is an equally important lesson. Do not label every CHUNK component an optimized design merely because the robot performed exceptionally. Borrow the output discipline and diagnose its failure modes; do not recreate a known weak load path without a correction hypothesis and impact test. Preserve version labels so an early divided shooter and later wider arrangement are not combined into an imaginary single fielded version. The owner's desire to emulate 7769 means elite execution of a coherent primary scorer, not a requirement for a particular hopper size, rack intake or lane count in 2027.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-7769-cad-tech-slides-chunk/521008 (posts 1,5,8); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-7769-cad-tech-slides-chunk/521008/15 ; https://www.thebluealliance.com/team/7769/2026 ; `tables/season_epa.jsonl`; existing `docs/research_continuation/2026-7769.md`. Tech slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/19V4ULNr7_ooZ6yJXtI6NRUoB1uEt86Wnw5UOy8DofH0/edit?usp=sharing — browser reports deleted. Existing interview reference https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6BrndIrOmgU remains source navigation, not a new watch in this pass.

## 1690, 2024 Doppler: compact primary scorer, substantial control development

Primary facts: the reveal gives an approximately 11-inch highest stowed point. Official results identify Orbit as a 2024 world champion. The mechanism is chassis-yaw aimed; its elevation/pivot motion is not a turret. In the CAD release, a team member warns that low packaging did not make every individual mechanism superior and that substantial work was needed. The team's controls explanation describes physically limited motion commands, skid/collision handling, driver assistance and automated shot readiness. Treat this as a team account rather than an independent performance decomposition.

1833 transfer analysis: low CG can increase usable acceleration and reduce settling, but free speed or stowed height alone cannot predict cycles. Compare time to accelerate, brake, reacquire heading, capture a piece and release a valid shot under contact. The cost of chassis aiming must be included in a non-turret architecture's state model. It may be small when acquisition exits with a useful heading and the driver can approach efficiently; it may be large when position and heading are constrained together. Geometry and software must be co-designed so that the driver requests remain physically feasible.

This example validates ambition with a compact architecture. It does not justify eliminating a necessary game function, assuming development is easy, or concluding that the lowest robot always wins. A low package that creates rare disabling piece poses may lose more match contribution than it gains in an ideal cycle. Preserve the existing note-deflector study as a reliability problem alongside the positive architecture example. The future design should carry an explicit optimization budget: time for loaded tuning, autonomous coordination, repeated defended acquisition, operator feedback and service drills. Hardware simplicity buys development capacity only if the saved effort is actually invested in those areas.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-presents-2024-robot-reveal-doppler/455350 (post 8); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838 (post 7); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-presents-2024-robot-reveal-doppler/455350/142 ; https://frc-events.firstinspires.org/2024/CMPTX/awards ; existing `docs/research_continuation/2024-1690.md`. No new CAD-dimensional certification.

## 2056, 2025 LIGHTNING: familiar functions, engineered interfaces

Primary facts: OP describes choosing architecture early and selecting the simplest concept it thought could meet competitive goals, while noting that the robot was more demanding than desired and lacked a hanger at its first event. Its 33-page binder documents a ground intake, separate coral straightening/handoff stages, elevator, gripper and climb, with explicit sensing, service and stiffness details. Software and fabrication are documented as part of the robot, not omitted from the complexity account. The existing corpus already contains five technical notes from this binder. In this pass all 33 pages' extracted text was read; that does not certify every drawing visually. The source publication requests that its original documents not be rehosted; this edition links them and retains authored research notes rather than adding the source PDF.

1833 transfer analysis: a concept can be stated as an intake, elevator and wrist without being an easy robot to commission. The high-level simplicity resides in a short functional chain with clear ownership of each transformation, not in pretending that orientation, capture or controls are trivial. Decompose a coral cycle into acquisition, orientation, handoff, clearance, elevation, approach, release and retreat. Observe which stages can overlap without compromising retained state. An indexed piece that arrives consistently can save both actuator travel and repeated driver correction.

The relevant design comparison is not vacuum versus rollers in isolation. It is whether the complete capture-to-release system tolerates the expected piece poses and contacts while achieving repeatable short cycles. Evaluate a simpler effector's potential benefit against the additional upstream alignment it demands. A more constrained handoff may reduce end-effector burden but increase throat-jam sensitivity. Deliberately choose where the tolerance belongs and measure success across that interface. Similarly, service access and wiring restraint are output-preserving design functions; a nominally faster mechanism that repeatedly loses sensors or requires lengthy disassembly can have lower event contribution.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550?page=2 (post 29 and controls discussion); https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf (physical pp 5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21,25,28); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550 (post 28). Exact construction remains in the five existing technical notes and primary publication.

## 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution

Primary facts: Orbit credits a closed-belt differential elevator reference and describes floor pickup as a cycle-time choice. Team posts identify pressure feedback and maintenance of an adhesive belt connection. Its championship recap discusses alliance interference and switching a partner to predictable loading-station lanes. A later intake-assist post explains driver-intent conditions and velocity correction. These accounts establish that optimization includes control and traffic management, not only a short mechanism list. They do not show that a differential or vacuum is universally simpler for another team.

1833 transfer analysis: separating moving hardware from actuator location can reduce inertia while creating motor-space coupling and calibration work. A differential should be assessed over simultaneous lift/pivot demands, saturation and failure recovery rather than judged by the number of motors saved. A vacuum can make a gripper visually small while moving complexity into sealing, pressure generation, state sensing and maintenance. Those are valid choices if they improve the whole cycle under the team's resources; they are not free complexity elimination.

For match modeling, faster individual floor pickup does not necessarily produce faster alliance throughput if robots fight over the same accessible pieces or routes. Compare shared supply and traffic policies explicitly. A robot designed to dominate can adopt a lane or temporary complementary assignment without having been designed as a weak support machine. The historical alliance discussion is therefore useful to 1833's elite ceiling even though support-only architecture is prohibited. Reserve time to test driver assistance at speed with realistic errors; a theoretically optimal command that surprises the driver may degrade acquisition. Observe driver workload and repeatability as well as mechanism motion time.

Prefer deleting a mechanism or powered interface when the same useful function can be achieved with fewer failure modes, but preserve a necessary capability even when it requires engineering. Invest saved complexity in sustained output, autonomous, acquisition quality, driver assistance, service readiness and iteration. Set measurable optimization experiments and retain the failures as prominently as the successes. Neither a simple concept nor a famous reference establishes performance until its interfaces and operating conditions have been evaluated.

title: DunkTank output failure analysis and 68-point historical review
body:
# DunkTank agent output review and regression case

The corrected assignment is 2024 WCP CADathon DunkTank. The earlier Hero Heist prompt attribution was corrected by the user, so it incurs no deduction. Reviewed artifacts: the user's supplied one-sheet task workbook and detailed design recommendation. Preserve their original state; this review is not a revised design or evidence of an implemented prototype.

The recorded review score is 68/100: assignment/context 9/10; rules/math 10/12; strategic model 8/14; task decomposition 7/10; workbook substance 7/10; reference quality 7/10; architecture 8/12; alternatives 2/8; tests 4/6; usefulness 6/8. This is an evidence-anchored reviewer judgment with ordinal partial credit, not a calibrated accuracy measurement. The subsequently supplied 1833 doctrine rejects a support-only architecture independently of that historical score.

Verified strengths: 58 tasks on one sheet; 43 Must do, 7 Might do, 8 Won't do; summary caches and priority-times-difficulty calculations match; no cached Excel error cells; final human decisions pending. Core stack math gives 48 ordinary basketball points, 60 possible final stack bonuses, a 31-point successful preload-plus-exit routine and 33 1/3 points for 100 successful endgame electrolyte scores. The packing calculation gives about 6.31 cubic feet at an assumed 60% fraction before mechanism intrusion. Those batch ceilings are not a match model. The output recognizes useful versus harmful clears, shared bonuses, ball return delay and intake-to-outlet integration.

Failure 1 — specialist selected before marginal comparison: two capable basketball partners are assumed, but no same-partner timed comparison establishes whether an electrolyte-only robot beats a mixed or basketball-capable candidate. Repair: model direct, enabled and denied output and a counterfactual replacement, including weak/ordinary and elite defended scenarios. For 1833, a support-only candidate is disallowed by the new owner instruction.

Failure 2 — threshold converted into capacity: row 25 makes 100 delivered onboard balls essential because the tank clears at a cumulative 100. Multiple smaller deliveries and existing tank inventory are not compared. Repair: evaluate capacities and fixed/expanding storage with travel, collection, mass/volume, losses and actual useful resets. Do not assert that a smaller design is necessarily better either.

Failure 3 — full refill used as denial proxy: final bonuses are evaluated per stack. An opponent that cannot refill all three can still restore one or two. Repair: model per-stack recovery, prerequisite dependencies, time left, and the attacker's lost scoring. Maximum 60 denied points is a conditional upper bound, not expected contribution.

Failure 4 — boilerplate dependencies: 50 of 58 J cells repeat the same coordination/route/timing sentence; the other eight repeat an exclusion sentence. Difficulty explanations similarly repeat that a number is provisional. Repair: require task-specific predecessor/interface/failure conditions and difficulty drivers. Task count and nonblank cells alone earn no substantive-quality credit.

Failure 5 — contradictory acceptance targets: row 25 requires at least 100 delivered; row 28 initially permits two residuals; row 56 requires 98% retention. Row 13 specifies 20/20 combined auto exits/discharges whereas rows 21/39 specify 18/20. Repair: define authoritative system release targets, screening stages, loss margins and test conditions, with traceable requirement IDs. Do not quietly label inconsistent targets equivalent.

Failure 6 — historical piece-size error: the recommendation describes 254's 2022 reference as 7-inch cargo. The official 2022 manual section 5.7 specifies 9.5-inch fuzzy inflated cargo. Repair: verify year-specific diameter, material and compliance before importing intake compression or contact speeds. The primary/secondary roller arrangement is supported by 254's binder; preserve the valid principle while correcting the dimensional statement.

Failure 7 — deferred physical feasibility and optimization: routes, field opening, packaging and resources are acknowledged unknown, but the output still selects capacity and expansion. Endgame/auto open-chute flow deserves investigation without assuming a physically accessible instant recycling loop. Repair: cheap aperture and envelope checks, state/flow model, capacity trade study, then integrated loaded tests. No complete new DunkTank recommendation is certified by adding this protocol.

Evidence locators: original workbook rows 13,21,25,28,32,39,56 and column J; detailed recommendation sections on hopper, compared alternative and first tests. Original uploaded attachments remain with the user and are not silently rewritten. Scoring criteria are in `agent/design_rubric.json`.

Sources: supplied DunkTank Game Update 01 manual, physical pp 3,10–14,17–19; https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wcp-cadathon-2024-dunktank/472262?page=4 ; https://firstfrc.blob.core.windows.net/frc2022/Manual/HTML/2022FRCGameManual.htm section 5.7; https://media.team254.com/2022/10/8f2407a5-Team_254_Tech_Binder_2022.pdf physical p14. Later update parity remains unverified. This case does not claim visual match watching or measured hardware results.


## Reproduction

Unchanged source artifacts are preserved in `evaluations/evidence/dunktank-2026-10-26/` from corpus root, with hashes in `data/dunktank_evidence_manifest.json`. Run `python scripts/audit_task_workbook.py evaluations/evidence/dunktank-2026-10-26/original_agent_task_list.xlsx`. The structural audit confirms 58 tasks and flags the 50 repeated dependency cells; it does not claim semantic correctness.

title: 2026-7769 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
body:
## 7769, 2026 CHUNK: flow, durability and honest failure history

Primary facts: the release describes a two-chamber shooter revised to a 2.75-width configuration, almost 70 nominal capacity and typically 50–60 in play. Team replies describe a static hood avoiding an exposed hood belt, and a feed jam corrected by stopping the lower indexing rollers. They also report rack-tooth breakage that persisted despite current-limit mitigation, with spares and repairs needed. Their linked technical slides currently display that the file was deleted. Those slides were not read. The retained mirror snapshot ranks 7769 fourth worldwide at EPA 309.29; it is a dated snapshot, not live verification. Official event results support an elite competitive season.

1833 transfer analysis: the useful principle is that usable match throughput is a system property. More capacity can add loaded inertia, acquisition dwell and feed pressure. More powered contact can make a congested path worse. Begin with a clear hypothesis about the limiting stage, instrument occupancy and delay at each transition, and change one stage before attributing a scoring gain. Test the near-empty, partly full and fully packed states separately. Under a defended shot, distinguish lost aim time, inaccessible geometry, supply starvation and a genuine mechanical jam. A simple hood can reduce interfaces and service work, but its advantages depend on the scoring aperture and collision environment of the new game.

The rack failure is an equally important lesson. Do not label every CHUNK component an optimized design merely because the robot performed exceptionally. Borrow the output discipline and diagnose its failure modes; do not recreate a known weak load path without a correction hypothesis and impact test. Preserve version labels so an early divided shooter and later wider arrangement are not combined into an imaginary single fielded version. The owner's desire to emulate 7769 means elite execution of a coherent primary scorer, not a requirement for a particular hopper size, rack intake or lane count in 2027.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-7769-cad-tech-slides-chunk/521008 (posts 1,5,8); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-7769-cad-tech-slides-chunk/521008/15 ; https://www.thebluealliance.com/team/7769/2026 ; `tables/season_epa.jsonl`; existing `docs/research_continuation/2026-7769.md`. title: 2024-1690 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
body:
## 1690, 2024 Doppler: compact primary scorer, substantial control development

Primary facts: the reveal gives an approximately 11-inch highest stowed point. Official results identify Orbit as a 2024 world champion. The mechanism is chassis-yaw aimed; its elevation/pivot motion is not a turret. In the CAD release, a team member warns that low packaging did not make every individual mechanism superior and that substantial work was needed. The team's controls explanation describes physically limited motion commands, skid/collision handling, driver assistance and automated shot readiness. Treat this as a team account rather than an independent performance decomposition.

1833 transfer analysis: low CG can increase usable acceleration and reduce settling, but free speed or stowed height alone cannot predict cycles. Compare time to accelerate, brake, reacquire heading, capture a piece and release a valid shot under contact. The cost of chassis aiming must be included in a non-turret architecture's state model. It may be small when acquisition exits with a useful heading and the driver can approach efficiently; it may be large when position and heading are constrained together. Geometry and software must be co-designed so that the driver requests remain physically feasible.

This example validates ambition with a compact architecture. It does not justify eliminating a necessary game function, assuming development is easy, or concluding that the lowest robot always wins. A low package that creates rare disabling piece poses may lose more match contribution than it gains in an ideal cycle. Preserve the existing note-deflector study as a reliability problem alongside the positive architecture example. The future design should carry an explicit optimization budget: time for loaded tuning, autonomous coordination, repeated defended acquisition, operator feedback and service drills. Hardware simplicity buys development capacity only if the saved effort is actually invested in those areas.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-presents-2024-robot-reveal-doppler/455350 (post 8); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/frc-orbit-1690-2024-robot-cad-release/464838 (post 7); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/orbit-1690-presents-2024-robot-reveal-doppler/455350/142 ; https://frc-events.firstinspires.org/2024/CMPTX/awards ; existing `docs/research_continuation/2024-1690.md`. title: 2025-2056 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
body:
## 2056, 2025 LIGHTNING: familiar functions, engineered interfaces

Primary facts: OP describes choosing architecture early and selecting the simplest concept it thought could meet competitive goals, while noting that the robot was more demanding than desired and lacked a hanger at its first event. Its 33-page binder documents a ground intake, separate coral straightening/handoff stages, elevator, gripper and climb, with explicit sensing, service and stiffness details. Software and fabrication are documented as part of the robot, not omitted from the complexity account. The existing corpus already contains five technical notes from this binder. In this pass all 33 pages' extracted text was read; that does not certify every drawing visually. The source publication requests that its original documents not be rehosted; this edition links them and retains authored research notes rather than adding the source PDF.

1833 transfer analysis: a concept can be stated as an intake, elevator and wrist without being an easy robot to commission. The high-level simplicity resides in a short functional chain with clear ownership of each transformation, not in pretending that orientation, capture or controls are trivial. Decompose a coral cycle into acquisition, orientation, handoff, clearance, elevation, approach, release and retreat. Observe which stages can overlap without compromising retained state. An indexed piece that arrives consistently can save both actuator travel and repeated driver correction.

The relevant design comparison is not vacuum versus rollers in isolation. It is whether the complete capture-to-release system tolerates the expected piece poses and contacts while achieving repeatable short cycles. Evaluate a simpler effector's potential benefit against the additional upstream alignment it demands. A more constrained handoff may reduce end-effector burden but increase throat-jam sensitivity. Deliberately choose where the tolerance belongs and measure success across that interface. Similarly, service access and wiring restraint are output-preserving design functions; a nominally faster mechanism that repeatedly loses sensors or requires lengthy disassembly can have lower event contribution.

Sources: https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550?page=2 (post 29 and controls discussion); https://2056.ca/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/OPR25-2056-Technical-Binder.pdf (physical pp 5,7,9,11,13,15,17,19,21,25,28); https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/team-2056-op-robotics-2025-technical-binder-release/502550 (post 28). Exact construction remains in the five existing technical notes and primary publication.

title: 2025-1690 optimization reference for elite simple architecture
body:
## 1690, 2025 WHISPER: compact functional description, coupled mechanics and execution

Primary facts: Orbit credits a closed-belt differential elevator reference and describes floor pickup as a cycle-time choice. Team posts identify pressure feedback and maintenance of an adhesive belt connection. Its championship recap discusses alliance interference and switching a partner to predictable loading-station lanes. A later intake-assist post explains driver-intent conditions and velocity correction. These accounts establish that optimization includes control and traffic management, not only a short mechanism list. They do not show that a differential or vacuum is universally simpler for another team.

1833 transfer analysis: separating moving hardware from actuator location can reduce inertia while creating motor-space coupling and calibration work. A differential should be assessed over simultaneous lift/pivot demands, saturation and failure recovery rather than judged by the number of motors saved. A vacuum can make a gripper visually small while moving complexity into sealing, pressure generation, state sensing and maintenance. Those are valid choices if they improve the whole cycle under the team's resources; they are not free complexity elimination.

For match modeling, faster individual floor pickup does not necessarily produce faster alliance throughput if robots fight over the same accessible pieces or routes. Compare shared supply and traffic policies explicitly. A robot designed to dominate can adopt a lane or temporary complementary assignment without having been designed as a weak support machine. The historical alliance discussion is therefore useful to 1833's elite ceiling even though support-only architecture is prohibited. Reserve time to test driver assistance at speed with realistic errors; a theoretically optimal command that surprises the driver may degrade acquisition. Observe driver workload and repeatability as well as mechanism motion time.
